claim: The zebrafish pronephric tubule has four discrete tubule segments: a proximal convoluted tubule (PCT), proximal straight tubule (PST), distal early (DE), and distal late (DL).
source: The zebrafish pronephric tubule has four discrete tubule segments: a proximal convoluted tubule (PCT), proximal straight tubule (PST), distal early (DE), and distal late (DL) (Wingert et al., 2007) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wingert et al., 2007, and is also illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The proximal segments of the zebrafish pronephros are homologous to the PCT and PST in mammals.
source: The proximal segments are homologous to the PCT and PST in mammals, while the distal segments are homologous to the mammalian thick ascending limb (TAL) and distal convoluted tubule (DCT), respectively (Wingert et al., 2007; Wingert and Davidson, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wingert et al., 2007 and Wingert and Davidson, 2008.

claim: The distal segments of the zebrafish pronephros are homologous to the mammalian thick ascending limb (TAL) and distal convoluted tubule (DCT).
source: The proximal segments are homologous to the PCT and PST in mammals, while the distal segments are homologous to the mammalian thick ascending limb (TAL) and distal convoluted tubule (DCT), respectively (Wingert et al., 2007; Wingert and Davidson, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wingert et al., 2007 and Wingert and Davidson, 2008.

claim: A chemical genetic screen using the Screen-Well ICCB Known Bioactives Library identified 78 out of 480 compounds (16.25%) that were associated with nephron phenotypes.
source: In total, 16.25% (78/480) of ICCB bioactives were associated with nephron phenotypes (Figure 1C, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data presented in Figure 1C and Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: Exposure to 1 mM 4-HPR led to an expansion of the PCT, caudal shift of the DE, and a dramatic expansion of the interval between these segments where the PST normally emerges.
source: Compared to WTs, exposure to 1 mM 4-HPR led to an expansion of the PCT, caudal shift of the DE, and a dramatic expansion of the interval between these segments where the PST normally emerges, suggestive of an expanded PST segment (Figure 1D) (Poureetezadi et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D and a citation to Poureetezadi et al., 2014.

claim: Exposure to bioactive prostaglandins PGD2, PGA1, PGJ2, and PGB2 was associated with changes in the pronephros whereby there was a reduced PCT segment length and a posterior shift in the position of the DE.
source: Exposure to these bioactive prostaglandins was associated with changes in the pronephros whereby there was a reduced PCT segment length and a posterior shift in the position of the DE, such that there was a noticeably longer domain between these segment regions compared to WT control embryos (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Exposure to dmPGE2 or PGB2 resulted in a dose-dependent increase in the domain length of the PST segment compared to WT embryos.
source: Exposure to dmPGE2 or PGB2 resulted in a dose-dependent increase in the domain length of the PST segment compared to WT embryos, visualized by WISH with the marker trpm7 (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—figure supplements 1,2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplements 1,2.

claim: Exposure to dmPGE2 or PGB2 resulted in a significant reduction in the length of the DL segment.
source: In conjunction with this change, the DL segment was significantly reduced in length, as visualized by WISH with the marker slc12a3 (Figure 2A,C, Figure 2—figure supplements 1,2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A,C and Figure 2—figure supplements 1,2.

claim: Exposure to dmPGE2 or PGB2 resulted in a dosage-dependent reduction of the rostral domain of the PCT.
source: Additionally, the rostral domain of the PCT was reduced in a dosage-dependent fashion, based on expression of slc20a1a (Figure 2A,D, Figure 2—figure supplements 1,2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A,D and Figure 2—figure supplements 1,2.

claim: There was a caudal shift in the position of the DE segment after dmPGE2 or PGB2 treatment, though its absolute length was unchanged.
source: Further, there was a caudal shift in the position of the DE segment though its absolute length was unchanged, based on expression of the DE-specific marker slc12a1, which resides between the domains of the PST and DL segments (Figure 2A,D, Figure 2—figure supplements 1,2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A,D and Figure 2—figure supplements 1,2.

claim: There were no statistical differences in the body axis length or pronephric domain between WT controls and dmPGE2 treated embryos.
source: We found no statistical differences in the body axis length or pronephric domain between WT controls and dmPGE2 treated embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Exposure of WT embryos to 30 μM indomethacin was associated with normal proximal segment locations along the embryonic trunk.
source: Exposure of WT embryos to 30 μM indomethacin was associated with normal proximal segment locations along the embryonic trunk (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The majority of embryos treated with 30 μM indomethacin developed an slc12a1-expressing DE segment that was significantly expanded in length.
source: However, the balance of distal segments was disrupted after indomethacin treatment, such that the majority of embryos developed an slc12a1-expressing DE segment that was significantly expanded in length and an slc12a3-expressing DL segment that was significantly reduced in length compared to wild-type controls (Figure 3A,B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A,B and C.

claim: The majority of embryos treated with 30 μM indomethacin developed an slc12a3-expressing DL segment that was significantly reduced in length compared to wild-type controls.
source: However, the balance of distal segments was disrupted after indomethacin treatment, such that the majority of embryos developed an slc12a1-expressing DE segment that was significantly expanded in length and an slc12a3-expressing DL segment that was significantly reduced in length compared to wild-type controls (Figure 3A,B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A,B and C.

claim: Treatment with the Ptgs1 (Cox1) selective inhibitor SC-560 induced an expansion of the DE segment and a restriction of the DL compared to wild-type embryos.
source: Treatment with the Ptgs1 (Cox1) selective inhibitor SC-560 or the Ptgs2a (Cox2) selective inhibitor NS-398 (Grosser et al., 2002; Cha et al., 2005; North et al., 2007) induced an expansion of the DE segment and a restriction of the DL compared to wild-type embryos, while having no discernible effect on proximal segment development (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2, and by citations to Grosser et al., 2002; Cha et al., 2005; North et al., 2007.

claim: Treatment with the Ptgs2a (Cox2) selective inhibitor NS-398 induced an expansion of the DE segment and a restriction of the DL compared to wild-type embryos.
source: Treatment with the Ptgs1 (Cox1) selective inhibitor SC-560 or the Ptgs2a (Cox2) selective inhibitor NS-398 (Grosser et al., 2002; Cha et al., 2005; North et al., 2007) induced an expansion of the DE segment and a restriction of the DL compared to wild-type embryos, while having no discernible effect on proximal segment development (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2, and by citations to Grosser et al., 2002; Cha et al., 2005; North et al., 2007.

claim: Single and double ptgs1/2a morphants developed a larger DE domain that was increased in length compared to WT control embryos.
source: Single and double ptgs1/2a morphants developed a larger DE domain that was increased in length compared to WT control embryos (Figure 4B–4D, Figure 4—figure supplements 1, 2 and 9).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4B–4D and Figure 4—figure supplements 1, 2 and 9.

claim: Single and double ptgs1/2a morphants had a shortened DL segment compared to the DL in WT control embryos.
source: In addition, single and double ptgs1/2a morphants had a shortened DL segment compared to the DL in WT control embryos (Figure 4B–4D, Figure 4—figure supplements 1, 2 and 9).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4B–4D and Figure 4—figure supplements 1, 2 and 9.

claim: PCT and PST segment development was normal in ptgs1, ptgs2a, or ptgs1/2a deficient embryos at the 24 hpf stage.
source: In contrast, PCT and PST segment development was normal in ptgs1, ptgs2a, or ptgs1/2a deficient embryos at the 24 hpf stage (Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: The alterations in DE and DL segments in ptgs1 and ptgs2a deficient embryos were rescued by exposure to dmPGE2.
source: We observed that the alterations in DE and DL segments in ptgs1 and ptgs2a deficient embryos were indeed rescued by exposure to dmPGE2, a treatment combination that was again not associated with altered proximal segment domains (Figure 4B,C, Figure 4—figure supplements 1, 2 and 9).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4B,C and Figure 4—figure supplements 1, 2 and 9.

claim: ptger2a transcripts were expressed in a continuous stretch of IM renal progenitors between the 12 ss and 24 ss.
source: Interestingly, we found that ptger2a transcripts were expressed in a continuous stretch of IM renal progenitors between the 12 ss and 24 ss based on their location in bilateral stripes of cells situated adjacent to the paraxial mesoderm (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4A.

claim: ptger4a transcripts were expressed in the IM renal fields between the 12 ss and 15 ss.
source: ptger4a transcripts were similarly expressed in the IM renal fields between the 12 ss and 15 ss, where cells expressed varying levels of signal, suggesting patches of somewhat variable expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4B.

claim: ptger4a transcripts showed low levels of ubiquitous mesoderm expression at the 20 ss, and then were localized to the cloaca region at the 24 ss.
source: ptger4a transcripts showed low levels of ubiquitous mesoderm expression at the 20 ss, and then were localized to the cloaca region at the 24 ss (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Deficiency of ptger2a or ptger4a resulted in a statistically significant expansion of the DE segment and a reduction of the DL.
source: Deficiency of ptger2a or ptger4a resulted in a statistically significant expansion of the DE segment and a reduction of the DL (Figure 4E,F, Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 5–9).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4E,F and Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 5–9.

claim: dmPGE2 was not sufficient to rescue either the DE segment expansion or DL reduction in ptger2a or ptger4a knockdown embryos.
source: We also specifically evaluated whether ptger2a or ptger4a knockdown could be rescued by dmPGE2, and found that dmPGE2 was not sufficient to rescue either the DE segment expansion or DL reduction (Figure 4—figure supplement 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 8.

claim: Indomethacin treatment from the 12 ss through to the 24 hpf time point elicited an expansion of the DE domain and a reduction of the DL similar to that seen from indomethacin treatments from 4 hpf to 24 hpf.
source: Indomethacin treatment during this time window elicited an expansion of the DE domain and a reduction of the DL similar to that seen from indomethacin treatments from 4 hpf to 24 hpf (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: dmPGE2 treatment from the 12 ss to 24 hpf was sufficient to induce an expansion of the PST and a reduction of the DL.
source: Further, dmPGE2 treatment from the 12 ss to 24 hpf was sufficient to induce an expansion of the PST and a reduction of the DL (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Treatments with either of two different Ptger2 small molecule antagonists, PF04418948 or AH6809, from the 12 ss to 24 hpf was sufficient to induce a statistically significant expansion of the DE segment and reduction of the DL segment compared to WT controls.
source: Interestingly, we also found that treatments with either of two different Ptger2 small molecule antagonists, PF04418948 or AH6809, from the 12 ss to 24 hpf was likewise sufficient to induce a statistically significant expansion of the DE segment and reduction of the DL segment compared to WT controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: dmPGE2 treatment led to a significant expansion of the sim1a and irx3b domains, along with a significant reduction of the mecom domain, in the majority of embryos.
source: Interestingly, we found that dmPGE2 treatment led to a significant expansion of the sim1a and irx3b domains, along with a significant reduction of the mecom domain, in the majority of embryos (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Indomethacin treatment led to no significant change in the sim1a domain, while the irx3b domain was significantly increased in absolute length and the mecom domain was significantly reduced in length.
source: Further, we found that indomethacin treatment led to no significant change in the sim1a domain, while the irx3b domain was significantly increased in absolute length and the mecom domain was significantly reduced in length (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Embryos that were treated with SC-560 concomitant with irx3b deficiency failed to form a DE segment, similar to irx3b deficiency alone.
source: Embryos that were treated with SC-560 concomitant with irx3b deficiency failed to form a DE segment, similar to irx3b deficiency alone (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: Prostaglandin signaling occurs upstream of irx3b to regulate DE segment development.
source: Taken together with the observation that indomethacin treatment was sufficient to expand the irx3b expression domain, this result is consistent with the conclusion that prostaglandin signaling occurs upstream of irx3b to regulate DE segment development.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the epistasis experiment showing that SC-560 treatment does not rescue irx3b morphant phenotype, combined with the observation that indomethacin expands irx3b expression.

claim: Overexpression of mecom at dosages ranging from 14–70 pg was not sufficient to alter DL segment fate in indomethacin treated embryos.
source: Overexpression of mecom at dosages ranging from 14–70 pg, in either the experimental or vehicle control group, was not sufficient to alter DL segment fate (Figure 7—figure supplement 1, data not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Knockdown of sim1a concomitant with dmPGE2 treatment led to an abrogation of the PST segment, similar to sim1a deficiency alone.
source: We found that knockdown of sim1a concomitant with dmPGE2 treatment led to an abrogation of the PST segment, similar to sim1a deficiency alone (Figure 7C,D, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7C,D and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: sim1a acts downstream of PGE2 signaling in the context of exogenous treatment to drive expansion of the PST segment.
source: These results are consistent with the conclusion that sim1a acts downstream of PGE2 signaling in the context of exogenous treatment to drive expansion of the PST segment.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the epistasis experiment showing that sim1a knockdown prevents dmPGE2-induced PST expansion.

claim: Vertebrate kidney organogenesis is a dynamic process involving the generation of up to three distinct structures that originate from the intermediate mesoderm (IM).
source: Vertebrate kidney organogenesis is a dynamic process involving the generation of up to three distinct structures that originate from the intermediate mesoderm (IM) (Saxen, 1987).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Saxen, 1987.

claim: In mammals, a pronephros, mesonephros, and metanephros develop in succession.
source: In mammals, a pronephros, mesonephros, and metanephros develop in succession.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammalian kidney development.

claim: The pronephros and mesonephros both eventually disintegrate in mammals, leaving the metanephros as the adult kidney.
source: Of these structures, the pronephros and mesonephros both eventually disintegrate, leaving the metanephros as the adult kidney.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mammalian kidney development.

claim: Lower vertebrates such as fish and amphibians only form a pronephros and mesonephros.
source: In contrast, lower vertebrates such as fish and amphibians only form a pronephros and mesonephros, which are active during embryogenesis and larval stages, respectively, and the mesonephros subsequently serves as the adult organ (Dressler, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dressler, 2006.

claim: The mesonephros serves as the adult kidney organ in lower vertebrates such as fish and amphibians.
source: In contrast, lower vertebrates such as fish and amphibians only form a pronephros and mesonephros, which are active during embryogenesis and larval stages, respectively, and the mesonephros subsequently serves as the adult organ (Dressler, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Dressler, 2006.

claim: Nephrons contain a renal corpuscle that filters the blood, a tubule that modifies the filtrate solution, and a collecting duct.
source: Nephrons contain a renal corpuscle that filters the blood, a tubule that modifies the filtrate solution, and a collecting duct (Romagnani et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Romagnani et al., 2013.

claim: The zebrafish embryonic pronephros is comprised of only two nephrons.
source: The zebrafish embryonic pronephros is a useful model to delineate the processes that regulate vertebrate nephron segmentation because it is anatomically simple, being comprised of only two nephrons (Gerlach and Wingert, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gerlach and Wingert, 2013.

claim: Renal progenitors arise rapidly from the IM and undergo a mesenchymal to epithelial transition (MET) to engender the tubule by 24 hr post fertilization (hpf) during zebrafish kidney development.
source: During zebrafish kidney development, renal progenitors arise rapidly from the IM and undergo a mesenchymal to epithelial transition (MET) to engender the tubule by 24 hr post fertilization (hpf) (McKee et al., 2014; Gerlach and Wingert, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to McKee et al., 2014 and Gerlach and Wingert, 2014.

claim: Renal progenitors undergo complex segment lineage patterning events, beginning with their segregation into rostral and caudal subdomains, a process that is orchestrated by the morphogen retinoic acid (RA) which is locally secreted by the adjacent paraxial mesoderm (PM).
source: Prior to this, the renal progenitors undergo complex segment lineage patterning events, beginning with their segregation into rostral and caudal subdomains, a process that is orchestrated by the morphogen retinoic acid (RA) which is locally secreted by the adjacent paraxial mesoderm (PM) (Wingert et al., 2007; Wingert and Davidson, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wingert et al., 2007 and Wingert and Davidson, 2011.

claim: Modulating levels of RA affects the specification of renal progenitors, inducing proximal segment lineage formation over distal.
source: Modulating levels of RA affects the specification of renal progenitors, inducing proximal segment lineage formation over distal, which can be accentuated by the addition of exogenous all-trans RA, while distal fates are induced over proximal by inhibiting endogenous production of RA through the application of the biosynthesis inhibitor N,N-diethlyaminobenzaldehyde (DEAB) (Wingert et al., 2007; Wingert and Davidson, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wingert et al., 2007 and Wingert and Davidson, 2011.

claim: Prostaglandins regulate many aspects of renal physiology in the adult kidney, ranging from tubular transport processes to hemodynamics.
source: With regard to the adult kidney, prostaglandins regulate many aspects of renal physiology, ranging from tubular transport processes to hemodynamics (Nasrallah et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nasrallah et al., 2007.

claim: There are five major prostaglandins produced from the precursor arachidonic acid (AA) by the enzymes Prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase one or Prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2a (Ptgs1 and Ptgs2a in zebrafish, also known as cyclooxygenases COX-1 and COX-2 in mammals) followed by subsequent processing by particular synthases.
source: More specifically, there are five major prostaglandins produced from the precursor arachidonic acid (AA) by the enzymes Prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase one or Prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2a (Ptgs1 and Ptgs2a in zebrafish, also known as cyclooxygenases COX-1 and COX-2 in mammals) followed by subsequent processing by particular synthases (Funk, 2001; Tootle, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Funk, 2001 and Tootle, 2013.

claim: PGE2 signals by interactions with Ptger G-protein coupled receptors including EP1, EP2, EP3 and EP4 (known as Ptger1-4 in zebrafish) on receiving cells.
source: PGE2 will signal by subsequent interactions with Ptger G-protein coupled receptors including EP1, EP2, EP3 and EP4 (known as Ptger1-4 in zebrafish) on receiving cells (Figure 1E) (Funk, 2001; Tootle, 2013; Yang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Funk, 2001; Tootle, 2013; Yang et al., 2013, and illustrated in Figure 1E.

claim: Genetic disruptions of components within the prostaglandin pathway in mice was associated with observably normal development, leading to the hypothesis that maternal prostaglandin sources had rescued embryogenesis.
source: Secondly, there is a substantial void in our understanding due to the results of murine loss of function studies where genetic disruptions of components within the prostaglandin pathway was associated with observably normal development. This led to the hypothesis that maternal prostaglandin sources had rescued embryogenesis, thereby complicating the use of mammalian models to study prostaglandin requirements during ontogeny.
evidence: This is a summary of historical findings in the field.

claim: COX-2 dosage is critical for murine metanephros development.
source: The importance of reevaluating prostaglandin signaling in kidney formation has been emphasized by a recent report that COX-2 dosage is critical for murine metanephros development, though it is presently enigmatic whether there are requirement(s) for discrete stages of nephrogenesis (Slattery et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Slattery et al., 2016.

claim: PGE2 regulates hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) development and function.
source: Most notably, there have been transformative revelations regarding the conserved roles of prostaglandin signaling during definitive blood formation, where PGE2 was found to regulate hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) development and function (North et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to North et al., 2007.

claim: PGE2 activity controls opposing cell fate decisions in the developing pancreas and liver through the ep4a receptor (also known as ptger4a).
source: A chemical genetic screen in zebrafish also identified the prostaglandin pathway as a modifier of endoderm organogenesis, where in subsequent work it was found that PGE2 activity controls opposing cell fate decisions in the developing pancreas and liver through the ep4a receptor (also known as ptger4a), which derive from a bipotential endoderm progenitor (Garnaas et al., 2012; Nissim et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Garnaas et al., 2012 and Nissim et al., 2014.

claim: Mice lacking COX-2 exhibit postnatal kidney pathologies associated with neonatal fatality, including nephron hypoplasia and atrophy, impaired cortical growth, and even cyst formation in multiple nephron segments.
source: Intriguingly, however, mice lacking COX-2 exhibit postnatal kidney pathologies associated with neonatal fatality, including nephron hypoplasia and atrophy, impaired cortical growth, and even cyst formation in multiple nephron segments—phenotypes suggestive of significant disruptions in renal ontogeny (Dinchuk et al., 1995; Morham et al., 1995; Mahler et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dinchuk et al., 1995; Morham et al., 1995; Mahler et al., 1996.

claim: COX-2+/- mice exhibit kidney insufficiency.
source: These observations were not further explored until recently, however, where COX-2 gene dosage and pharmacological inhibition were linked to renal defects in glomerular size, such that COX-2+/- mice were found to exhibit kidney insufficiency (Slattery et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Slattery et al., 2016.

claim: Exposure to COX inhibitors like indomethacin during human development is associated with renal failure, where the histological aspects include small glomeruli and microcystic lesions among other defects.
source: In alignment with these data, exposure to COX inhibitors like indomethacin during human development is associated with renal failure, where the histological aspects include small glomeruli and microcystic lesions among other defects (Gloor et al., 1993; van der Heijden et al., 1994; Kaplan et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Gloor et al., 1993; van der Heijden et al., 1994; Kaplan et al., 1994.

claim: Prostaglandin signaling, likely through PGE2, has critical roles in nephrogenesis.
source: In light of these recent observations along with our findings, we propose that prostaglandin signaling, likely through PGE2, has critical roles in nephrogenesis, which warrant further investigation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the integration of prior literature and the current study's findings.

claim: PGE2 is currently in phase two clinical trials for increasing the efficiency of bone marrow transplants.
source: PGE2 is currently in phase two clinical trials for increasing the efficiency of bone marrow transplants (Hagedorn et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hagedorn et al., 2014.

claim: PGE2 was shown to be a regulator of bipotential endoderm cell fate decisions in development for zebrafish and mouse endodermal cells.
source: Furthermore, PGE2 was shown to be a regulator of bipotential endoderm cell fate decisions in development for zebrafish and mouse endodermal cells (Nissim et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nissim et al., 2014.

claim: PGE2 activity later in organ formation induced proliferation of both the liver and pancreas buds.
source: Curiously, it was also shown that PGE2 activity later in organ formation induced proliferation of both the liver and pancreas buds.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from prior research.

claim: Blocking ptger2a promoted liver versus pancreas specification.
source: This change in the function of PGE2 is explained by the spatial and temporal expression of ptger2a and ptger4a, where blocking ptger2a promoted liver versus pancreas specification and blocking ptger4a promoted the outgrowth of the liver and pancreas buds.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from prior research.

claim: Blocking ptger4a promoted the outgrowth of the liver and pancreas buds.
source: This change in the function of PGE2 is explained by the spatial and temporal expression of ptger2a and ptger4a, where blocking ptger2a promoted liver versus pancreas specification and blocking ptger4a promoted the outgrowth of the liver and pancreas buds.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from prior research.
